title: Repeat card usage
objective: Customers who used the card once have not come back. Encourage a second and third transaction.
reviewerNotes: There is no 'used once' event, so this is an audience question answered with transaction history, not an event entry. The agent should notice the difference.
watchFor: no acknowledgement that recency must be expressed as a lookback

questions: The objective names both a second AND a third transaction, but a campaign has one goal and auto-exits once it's reached. Should this build target only the 2nd transaction (recommended, with a separate mirrored campaign later for 2nd→3rd), or do you want a different structure?

strategy.summary: Target customers whose only recorded activity is one customer-initiated, settled transaction, and nudge them toward a second use with a short, escalating-channel sequence. The platform can't prove 'used exactly once' directly (no transaction-count attribute exists), so entry fires on any qualifying transaction and relies on single-enrollment-per-campaign behaviour to approximate first-time users. The goal is the next qualifying transaction, which proves the comeback behaviour; driving a third transaction is a separate, follow-on concern since one campaign has one goal and exits on reaching it.
approach: Entry on a customer-initiated, settled/approved Transaction event rather than Card Activated — activation proves the card works, not that spend happened, so it would enter people too early and miss the actual gap (one txn, no more).

Goal is the next customer-initiated settled/approved Transaction — that is the only event that proves 'came back', and it sits on a different occurrence of the same event type than entry, so it is not trivially pre-satisfied.
Lead with EMAIL (lowest cost) for the first-touch, move to SMS for the reminder, reserve WHATSAPP (highest cost) for the final recovery nudge, per the lead-with-lower-cost preference.
Cap at 3 sends (within the 4-message limit) with 48h+ spacing, reflecting the conservative 'fewer, better-targeted messages' preference rather than maxing out the cap.
10% control group held out, since any read of 'did this help' needs a holdout; no lift numbers are claimed anywhere in this design.

rejected.why: Proves the card is usable, not that only one transaction has occurred; would enter people before or regardless of the actual single-use problem.
Conservative risk appetite prefers fewer, targeted messages; with no performance history to compare against, an experiment adds complexity without a clear decision it would inform yet.
A fourth message this soon risks fatigue (P-011) for an outcome that has no deadline forcing urgency; 3 is enough to test the hypothesis.

assumptions: The campaign platform enrolls each customer once per campaign (does not re-trigger entry on every subsequent transaction); this is what makes 'first transaction' targeting workable at all given no count attribute exists.
A 2-week messaging window (first send ~48h after the qualifying transaction, final nudge by day ~9-10) is a reasonable test horizon with no hard deadline forcing urgency, unlike an EMI offer.

This campaign's single goal is the second transaction; prompting a third transaction is treated as a separate, mirrored follow-on campaign rather than a 4th step after this goal, since reaching the goal auto-exits the journey.
evidenceNotes: No performance history exists for this bank (stated in brief), so channel order, spacing and copy are hypotheses, not predictions.
Aggregated time-to-second-transaction data, if it existed, would help size the wait/window better than the 2-week default assumed here — noted as a gap, not a blocker.

steps.name: Welcome back nudge
steps.copy: Hi ${customerFirstName}, thanks for making your first purchase with your IndusInd card! Keep using it and you start earning rewards on everyday spends. See what you could earn next.

steps.name: Reminder nudge
steps.copy: ${customerFirstName}, your IndusInd card has more to give. Use it again on everyday spends like groceries or dining to start earning cashback.

steps.name: Final recovery nudge
steps.copy: Still haven't used your card again, ${customerFirstName}? Pick up where you left off, groceries, dining and more all earn rewards every time you pay with it.

turns.reply:
Target customers whose only recorded activity is one customer-initiated, settled transaction, and nudge them toward a second use with a short, escalating-channel sequence. The platform can't prove 'used exactly once' directly (no transaction-count attribute exists), so entry fires on any qualifying transaction and relies on single-enrollment-per-campaign behaviour to approximate first-time users. The goal is the next qualifying transaction, which proves the comeback behaviour; driving a third transaction is a separate, follow-on concern since one campaign has one goal and exits on reaching it.

**Approach**
- Entry on a customer-initiated, settled/approved Transaction event rather than Card Activated — activation proves the card works, not that spend happened, so it would enter people too early and miss the actual gap (one txn, no more).
- Goal is the next customer-initiated settled/approved Transaction — that is the only event that proves 'came back', and it sits on a different occurrence of the same event type than entry, so it is not trivially pre-satisfied.
- Lead with EMAIL (lowest cost) for the first-touch, move to SMS for the reminder, reserve WHATSAPP (highest cost) for the final recovery nudge, per the lead-with-lower-cost preference.
- Cap at 3 sends (within the 4-message limit) with 48h+ spacing, reflecting the conservative 'fewer, better-targeted messages' preference rather than maxing out the cap.
- 10% control group held out, since any read of 'did this help' needs a holdout; no lift numbers are claimed anywhere in this design.

**Considered and not used**
- Entry on Card Activated/Card Issued — Proves the card is usable, not that only one transaction has occurred; would enter people before or regardless of the actual single-use problem.
- An experiment (A/B) on channel order — Conservative risk appetite prefers fewer, targeted messages; with no performance history to compare against, an experiment adds complexity without a clear decision it would inform yet.
- Using the full 4-message cap — A fourth message this soon risks fatigue (P-011) for an outcome that has no deadline forcing urgency; 3 is enough to test the hypothesis.

**Assumptions**
- The campaign platform enrolls each customer once per campaign (does not re-trigger entry on every subsequent transaction); this is what makes 'first transaction' targeting workable at all given no count attribute exists.
- A 2-week messaging window (first send ~48h after the qualifying transaction, final nudge by day ~9-10) is a reasonable test horizon with no hard deadline forcing urgency, unlike an EMI offer.
- This campaign's single goal is the second transaction; prompting a third transaction is treated as a separate, mirrored follow-on campaign rather than a 4th step after this goal, since reaching the goal auto-exits the journey.

**Worth settling before this is built**
- The objective names both a second AND a third transaction, but a campaign has one goal and auto-exits once it's reached. Should this build target only the 2nd transaction (recommended, with a separate mirrored campaign later for 2nd→3rd), or do you want a different structure? Determines whether this is one campaign or two, and what 'success' means for this build. Until then: Proceed with this campaign's goal as the second transaction; propose a follow-on campaign for the third transaction as a later, separate build.

**Defaults applied**
- Is there a natural deadline or seasonal window for this reactivation push (e.g., tie to a statement cycle), or is a flat ~2-week window fine? A real deadline would let the copy say something more concrete (e.g., 'before your next statement') and could compress or extend spacing. Until then: Default to a ~2-week window with 3 messages at 48h+/96h+/120h+ spacing, with no explicit deadline language in copy.

**Limitations**
- Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
- No attribute exposes a customer's transaction count, so the platform cannot literally filter 'exactly one transaction ever' at entry — it can only trigger on a qualifying transaction event and rely on single-entry-per-campaign enrollment to approximate first-time users. If this campaign is re-enterable, customers well past their second or third transaction could also receive 'come back' messaging that doesn't match their situation.
